Sweet Pineapple and Raisin Tamales

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Makes 25-30 tamalesPrep 1 hour 30 minCook 1 hour 15 min

Sweet Pineapple and Raisin Tamales are a delightful and comforting treat, often enjoyed during festive seasons in Mexico. While La Noche de Rabanos in Oaxaca is famous for its radish carvings, these sweet tamales offer a warm, traditional culinary experience, perfect for sharing with family and friends during the holiday celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 50-60 dried corn husks
  • 4 cups (480 g) masa harina for tamales
  • 1 1/2 cups (340 g) lard or vegetable shortening, softened
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 3 1/2 to 4 cups (840-960 ml) pineapple juice or warm water
  • 1 (20-ounce / 567 g) can crushed pineapple, well drained
  • 1 cup (150 g) golden raisins
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar (adjust to taste)
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon

Method

  1. Place the dried corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover with hot water, and let them soak for at least 1 hour, or until they are pliable. Rinse them well and drain.
  2. In a very large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the softened lard or vegetable shortening until it is light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
  3. Add the 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt to the lard mixture and continue to beat until well combined.
  4. Gradually add the masa harina, alternating with the pineapple juice or warm water, beating until a soft, spreadable dough forms. The masa should be light and fluffy; a small piece should float in a glass of cold water when dropped in.
  5. In a separate medium bowl, combine the well-drained crushed pineapple, golden raisins, 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon. Mix thoroughly.
  6. To assemble the tamales, take one softened corn husk, with the wider end at the top. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider part of the husk, leaving a border of about 1 inch (2.5 cm) on the sides and 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) at the narrow end.
  7. Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the pineapple and raisin filling in the center of the masa.
  8. Fold one side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other side over, overlapping. Fold the narrow end of the husk up towards the center to seal the tamale.
  9. Repeat with the remaining masa, filling, and husks until all tamales are assembled.
  10. Arrange the tamales upright (open end up) in a steamer basket. Do not pack them too tightly, allowing steam to circulate.
  11. Fill the steamer pot with water up to just below the basket. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the masa pulls away easily from the husk.
  12. Let the tamales rest for 10-15 minutes off the heat before serving.

Tips

  • For an extra aromatic touch, add 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla extract to the masa mixture.
  • If you prefer, you can use milk instead of pineapple juice or water for a richer masa.
  • Sweet tamales can be made ahead of time, refrigerated for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat them by steaming until warmed through.
